account: There may be some quiet preparations under way, but I have not established what they are for. At tea, my neighbour said Townsfolk 02 had mentioned lights or decorations at the bakery. This is secondhand and unconfirmed: the neighbour also said the baker knew of no special occasion. I have not personally inspected any decorations. The neighbour had heard the builder seeking a private meeting with the innkeeper. This evening I personally heard the innkeeper invite the builder to the inn for a private supplies discussion, and the builder has now moved toward the inn. That could simply be ordinary business; I do not know whether it connects to the decoration report. My attempts to ask the builder about work and supplies were not heard by him, so his lack of an answer is not evidence of evasiveness. The innkeeper has arranged a meeting with me tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the great hall about the inn's business, now repeatedly confirmed, and says I need prepare nothing. He has not explained the substance. Separately, the town accounts were unavailable today; the secretary found all four great hall tables empty and knows of no papers brought in. There is no evidence tying that administrative gap to the other conversations. My best tentative guess is either routine inn supply arrangements or preparations for some pleasant occasion, possibly involving the bakery, builder, and innkeeper. A secret celebration is only a possibility, not a discovery. I should learn more through ordinary conversations and keep tomorrow's appointments rather than treat these fragments as proof of wrongdoing.
